newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions, gov't to resume labor talks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions, gov't to resume labor talks.

text.p: Argentine union and government officials plan to resume talks next week on labor reforms and workers health plans -- issues behind two of last year's three general strikes.
Union officials said CGT union federation leader Rodolfo Daer has accepted an invitation from cabinet chief Jorge Rodriguez to resume talks.
"We won't say no to talks with the government," a CGT spokesman said.

President Carlos Menem's administration, which had taken a tough line with unions, extended an olive branch to the labor confederation after two judges blocked its attempts to implement by decree labor reforms its considers vital to combatting unemployment 17.3 percent.
Menem resorted to decrees in the face of opposition in Congress and a breakdown in talks with unions, who fear the labor and health plan reforms will undercut their power.

The decrees, now frozen by judges, would allow workers to choose their union health plan, let smaller firms bypass national unions in collective pay talks and let firms appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.

The CGT has called the attempt to rule by decree a sign of "impotence founded on incompetence." The union campaign was reinforced Tuesday by the hardline MTA union faction's decision not to carry out its threat to break with the CGT -- as long as the fight against labor reform continues.
